long_biography.plain_text:
Sallas trained as an economist in Athens and Heidelberg, then combined academic work with institutional roles in Greece's financial system. He founded a portfolio-investment company in 1989 and, two years later, led a group of investors in acquiring the state-controlled Piraeus Bank. As chairman, he used repeated acquisitions and integration to turn a small lender into one of Greece's largest banking groups.

He left Piraeus in 2016 and returned to bank ownership through Lyktos Group's strategic investment in Pancreta Bank, before selling that stake. Lyktos then developed into a broader investment platform, backing energy storage, aquaculture, pharmaceutical production, tourism and asset management. The shift preserved Sallas's founder-led capital-allocation role while moving his current interests beyond the banking sector that defined his earlier career.
